# The RTL-to-GDSII Flow

## Concepts

The ASIC flow turns a verified RTL description into a physical implementation using a selected process design kit and libraries. Its stages include synthesis, floorplanning, power distribution, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, parasitic extraction, timing analysis, and physical checks.

Different views serve different consumers:

| View | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Verilog netlist/model | Connectivity or simulation |
| Liberty | Cell or macro timing and power characterization |
| LEF | Abstract geometry, pins, and routing obstructions |
| DEF | Placed design and routing information |
| GDSII | Detailed layout geometry |
| SDC | Timing constraints |
| SPEF | Extracted interconnect parasitics |

Producing GDSII is an implementation milestone. Review timing, DRC, LVS, and integration requirements before treating the block as ready for a larger design or fabrication.

## Implementation

Begin with UART loopback as a small physical-design case, then apply the workflow to larger SoC blocks. Freeze the RTL revision, parameters, PDK/library versions, clock constraints, and configuration for every run.

Soft IP includes RTL, tests, constraints, and documentation. An ASIC-hardened block also needs physical and timing views plus evidence that its checks passed under stated conditions. Memory macros require wrappers and compatible simulation/physical views.

## Hands-on Experiments

Package one implemented block so another engineer can reproduce and integrate it. Include interface and reset contracts, configuration, verification status, timing summary, layout/check results, and known limitations.

Audit the package for missing macro views, unjustified timing exceptions, stale reports, and absolute machine-specific paths. Distinguish requirements that passed from requirements that were not checked.
